newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq, Turkey to start building gas pipeline soon.
newsitem.headline: Iraq, Turkey to start building gas pipeline soon.

text.p: Iraq and Turkey will soon start building a gas pipeline to carry Iraqi exports to the Mediterranean, the government newspaper al-Jumhouriya reported on Tuesday.

The paper, quoting Talal Ashour director-general of the Northern Oil Company, said the pipeline project, stretching for 1,300 kilometres (800 miles), consists of three phases and the first entails the development of five gas fields in the country.

Iraqi and Turkish officials signed on May 10 a preliminary deal to construct the $2.7 billion pipeline but they did not say when they expected the work to begin or how long it would take to complete it.
Jumhouriya said the second stage will include the construction of the pipeline in both Iraq and Turkey and the third will compose the building of necessary annexes.
The paper said the production capacity of the project will be 10 million cubic metres of gas (33 million cubic feet) per year.
Under the deal the pipeline would provide Turkey with gas in return for meeting Iraqi needs for products such as food.

Iraq is allowed to export limited amounts of oil worth $2 billion in six months. The removal of total ban on oil exports largely depends on Iraq coming clean on its weapons of mass destruction banned under the 1991 Gulf War cease-fire.
Official estimates put proven gas reserves at more than 3,115 billion cubic metres (10,217 billion cubic feet) in 1989.
